answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity stake a refundable work-bond before it transacts: a newcomer must finish paid, verifiable jobs for strangers, and every reputation point is a pigment drawn from countersigned receipts, never self-claims. A thousand puppet accounts each owe that bond and those burn-in hours, so fakery costs linear capital and labour, not one cheap signup. Like vessels that must unload cargo at the wharf before docking at the jetty, standing comes from delivered work, and a sybil fleet pays in full for every hull.
